overview.executive_summary: Today's verified candidates highlight widespread infrastructure risk, AI-enabled attacks, major data breaches, and significant law-enforcement and regulatory action.

sections.heading: Windows Server 2016 support deadline
sections.what_happened: Microsoft reminded customers that Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates in 60 days.
sections.why_it_matters: Organizations still running the platform may face increasing security exposure after support ends.
sections.recommended_attention: Identify remaining deployments and plan migration or compensating controls.

sections.heading: Coles investigates cyber incident
sections.what_happened: Australian retailer Coles said it is investigating a cybersecurity incident that has not affected its stores.
sections.why_it_matters: The investigation could reveal operational or data risks for a major retailer.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor official updates and assess possible customer or business impact.

sections.heading: NoisyTCP Linux vulnerability
sections.what_happened: An 11-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability reportedly affects almost all Linux distributions and can crash systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH with default configurations.
sections.why_it_matters: The broad exposure and denial-of-service potential affect commonly deployed internet-facing services.
sections.recommended_attention: Review kernel exposure and prioritize mitigation for public-facing Linux systems.

sections.heading: Windows emergency activation updates
sections.what_happened: Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates to fix Windows activation and licensing failures caused by this month's security updates.
sections.why_it_matters: Activation failures can disrupt otherwise functioning Windows environments.
sections.recommended_attention: Validate affected systems and apply the emergency updates through normal change controls.

sections.heading: FBI warning on ARTEX AI hacking tool
sections.what_happened: The FBI warned that attackers are using the AI-powered ARTEX penetration-testing framework to automate global cyberattacks, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach.
sections.why_it_matters: Automated attack tooling may increase the scale and speed of compromises affecting Microsoft 365 environments.
sections.recommended_attention: Review supply-chain exposure, identity controls, and unusual automated activity.

sections.heading: TSMC employee data breach
sections.what_happened: TSMC confirmed that personal employee data was leaked online after a threat actor offered 6.9 gigabytes of allegedly stolen information for auction.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident creates potential privacy, fraud, and employee-targeting risks.
sections.recommended_attention: Watch for further disclosures and reinforce protections around affected personnel.

sections.heading: Cursor marketplace compromise
sections.what_happened: Cursor said a breach enabled hackers to distribute a malicious Claude Code extension after credentials were stolen from Fireworks AI.
sections.why_it_matters: Compromised developer extensions can provide a direct route into software-development environments.
sections.recommended_attention: Review installed extensions, marketplace trust, and credentials connected to development tooling.

sections.heading: North Korean campaign disrupted
sections.what_happened: The U.S. government disrupted the FaceStealer social-engineering campaign, which was responsible for stealing more than 400 million dollars in cryptocurrency.
sections.why_it_matters: The scale demonstrates the financial impact of sustained social-engineering operations.
sections.recommended_attention: Strengthen defenses against impersonation, credential theft, and cryptocurrency fraud.

sections.heading: SANSAR Linux cryptomining malware
sections.what_happened: A financially motivated cluster used SANSAR, a Rust-based toolkit that communicates over the Tor anonymity network and modifies NVIDIA library readings to hide high graphics-processing-unit workloads.
sections.why_it_matters: Stealthy mining can consume infrastructure resources while evading performance-based detection.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor graphics-processing-unit activity and integrity of relevant system libraries.

sections.heading: AI agents target exposed AI applications
sections.what_happened: Amazon reported that attackers' AI agents searched internet-exposed LiteLLM, One API, Dify, and other applications for provider keys, then used stolen keys to run models that helped search for more keys.
sections.why_it_matters: Exposed AI services can become both targets and tools in an automated theft cycle.
sections.recommended_attention: Protect provider keys, remove unnecessary internet exposure, and audit AI application configurations.

sections.heading: BO Team compromises code-signing infrastructure
sections.what_happened: Kaspersky's ICS CERT documented a months-long BO Team compromise of a Russian software developer's network that included development infrastructure and a code-signing server, using Log4Shell in VMware vCenter.
sections.why_it_matters: A compromised code-signing server can threaten the trustworthiness of distributed software.
sections.recommended_attention: Review legacy Log4Shell exposure, signing infrastructure, and build-system integrity.

sections.heading: Italy fines Meta over gallery access
sections.what_happened: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta 805 million euros over a Facebook for Android feature that accessed users' gallery content and metadata without explicit consent.
sections.why_it_matters: The decision underscores regulatory and privacy risks from default access to sensitive mobile data.
sections.recommended_attention: Review mobile permissions, consent flows, and privacy controls for comparable features.

stories.title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in 60 days
stories.summary: Microsoft reminded customers that Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates after reaching end of support in two months.
stories.why_it_matters: Organizations that do not migrate may be left without security updates for a widely used server platform.

stories.title: Australian retail giant Coles investigates cybersecurity incident
stories.summary: Coles Group Limited is investigating a cybersecurity incident and said its stores have not been impacted.
stories.why_it_matters: The investigation concerns a major retailer and could develop into a broader operational or data-security event.

stories.title: New NoisyTCP vulnerability lets attackers crash Linux servers
stories.summary: An 11-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability reportedly affects almost all Linux distributions and can crash systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH with default configurations.
stories.why_it_matters: The breadth of affected systems and ability to crash common services make this a significant availability risk.

stories.title: Microsoft pushes Windows emergency updates to fix activation failures
stories.summary: Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates to fix Windows activation and licensing failures caused by this month's security updates.
stories.why_it_matters: Activation failures can disrupt access to otherwise functioning Windows systems.

stories.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
stories.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation warned that attackers are using the AI-powered ARTEX penetration-testing framework to automate attacks worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach.
stories.why_it_matters: Automated offensive tooling may increase attack scale and affect Microsoft 365 customer environments.

stories.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
stories.summary: TSMC confirmed that personal employee data was leaked online after a threat actor offered 6.9 gigabytes of allegedly stolen information for auction.
stories.why_it_matters: The disclosure creates potential privacy and employee-targeting risks for a major semiconductor company.

stories.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
stories.summary: Cursor confirmed that hackers used a breach involving credentials stolen from Fireworks AI to distribute a malicious Claude Code extension through its marketplace.
stories.why_it_matters: A malicious developer extension can compromise users and software-development environments through a trusted distribution channel.

stories.title: US disrupts North Korean campaign behind $400 million crypto theft
stories.summary: The U.S. government disrupted the FaceStealer social-engineering campaign, which was responsible for stealing more than 400 million dollars in cryptocurrency.
stories.why_it_matters: The operation shows the substantial financial consequences of sustained social-engineering campaigns.

stories.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
stories.summary: A financially motivated cluster used SANSAR, a Rust-based orchestrator that communicates over the Tor anonymity network and modifies NVIDIA library readings to hide graphics-processing-unit workloads.
stories.why_it_matters: The concealment technique can help cryptomining remain undetected on Linux systems.

stories.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
stories.summary: Amazon said attackers' AI agents searched exposed AI applications for provider keys, then used stolen keys to run models that helped search for more keys.
stories.why_it_matters: Poorly protected AI applications can enable an automated cycle of credential theft and further attack activity.

stories.title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server
stories.summary: Kaspersky's ICS CERT documented a months-long BO Team compromise of a Russian software developer's network, including development infrastructure and a code-signing server, after exploitation of Log4Shell in VMware vCenter.
stories.why_it_matters: Compromised signing infrastructure can undermine trust in software distributed to customers.

stories.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
stories.summary: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta 805 million euros over a Facebook for Android feature that accessed users' gallery content and metadata without explicit consent.
stories.why_it_matters: The decision highlights the regulatory consequences of default access to sensitive mobile data.

tts.text: Here is today’s cybersecurity briefing. Microsoft says Windows Server 2016 will reach end of support in 60 days, so organizations should identify remaining systems and plan their migration. A serious Linux kernel issue called NoisyTCP can crash servers running common services such as Nginx, Apache, and SSH. Microsoft also issued emergency updates for Windows activation failures caused by recent security updates. The Federal Bureau of Investigation, or FBI, warned that the AI-powered ARTEX tool is helping automate attacks, including a ConnectWise supply-chain breach. TSMC confirmed that employee data was leaked, while Coles is investigating a cyber incident. Cursor said stolen Fireworks AI credentials enabled a malicious Claude Code extension. Authorities disrupted the North Korean FaceStealer campaign after more than 400 million dollars in cryptocurrency theft. Amazon reported AI agents searching exposed applications for provider keys. Finally, SANSAR hides Linux cryptomining activity, and a BO Team intrusion reached a code-signing server. Italy also fined Meta 805 million euros over Android gallery access without explicit consent.
